stem: Meera's father has fitted a convex mirror at the gate of their apartment building in Pune so that the security guard can watch a wide stretch of the road. Why is a convex mirror used here instead of a plane mirror?

options.text: It forms an image larger than the object, so vehicles look bigger.
It forms a real, inverted image that can be seen clearly at night.
It gives an erect, smaller image and a wider field of view of the road.
It reflects sunlight better, so it needs no electricity.

teacher.key_rationale: A convex mirror always forms erect, diminished images and has a wide field of view, which is why it suits surveillance and road-safety use; option C states both features. Options A, B and D describe properties convex mirrors do not have.
